title: Cannoli Siciliani
subtitle: sicilian pastry tubes with sweetened ricotta filling
excerpt: Cannoli Siciliani are crisp fried pastry shells filled with sweetened ricotta, candied peel and chopped pistachios. The shells are made from a marsala-enriched dough that is rolled thin, wrapped around metal tubes and fried until blistered and golden. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Cannoli are one of the oldest Sicilian pastries, with roots in the Arab-Norman period of the island. They were originally made for Carnevale but are now eaten year-round. The name comes from the word for 'tube' and refers to the cane reeds that were historically used as moulds.

content.text: are the most iconic of all Sicilian pastries: crisp fried tubes filled at the last minute with sweetened

cream. The shell dough includes marsala wine and butter, which together create the characteristic blistered surface during frying. This recipe serves 4 and makes around 12 shells, which is plenty for three per person.

The filling must be piped in just before serving. If the shells are filled in advance they will soften and lose their crunch. The shells themselves can be made a day ahead and stored in an airtight tin.

Make the dough. Combine the flour, caster sugar and cinnamon in a bowl. Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Add the marsala a little at a time, mixing until a smooth, firm dough forms. Knead for 2 minutes, wrap in cling film and rest in the fridge for 1 hour.
While the dough rests, make the filling. Beat the drained ricotta with the icing sugar until smooth. Fold in the candied peel. Chill until needed.
On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough very thin, to about 2mm. Cut out circles roughly 10cm in diameter. Wrap each circle around a cannoli tube, sealing the edge with a little water.

Pour enough olive oil or a neutral frying oil into a large, deep frying pan to reach a depth of 5cm. Heat to 180C. Fry the shells 3 or 4 at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until deep golden and blistered all over. Drain on kitchen paper and leave to cool before sliding off the tubes.
When ready to serve, spoon the ricotta filling into a piping bag fitted with a plain nozzle. Pipe the filling into both ends of each shell until it meets in the middle.
Press chopped pistachios into each end of the filling. Dust generously with icing sugar and serve within 20 minutes of filling.

attrs.symptom: Shells are not blistering during frying
attrs.fix: Use a thermometer to hold the oil at 180C; below this temperature the shells absorb oil and stay pale rather than blistering

attrs.symptom: Filling is watery and collapses out of the shell
attrs.cause: Ricotta was not drained long enough before using
attrs.fix: Drain ricotta in a fine sieve over a bowl in the fridge overnight; it should be thick and paste-like when ready to use

attrs.symptom: Shells are soggy by the time they reach the table
attrs.cause: They were filled too far in advance
attrs.fix: Fill cannoli no more than 20 minutes before serving; the shells can be fried and stored in a tin for up to 24 hours unfilled

content.text: Cannoli are sold from pastry shops across Sicily, filled to order in front of the customer. In Palermo they are eaten standing at the counter with a coffee. The quality varies enormously depending on how long ago they were filled. A cannolo filled hours before eating is a different and inferior thing. Make them at home and fill them just before serving.
